note: Europe at the end of 1955. The Federal Republic of Germany joined NATO and the German Democratic Republic joined the Warsaw Pact; the Warsaw Pact was founded in May. Austria regained sovereignty and declared permanent neutrality, while the Saar Protectorate remained separate pending its later union with West Germany. Berlin and Vienna are shown as whole regions rather than divided sectors, and modern administrative regions approximate several borders.

East Germany
properties.info: The German Democratic Republic was established in 1949 and joined the Warsaw Pact in 1955. Berlin is shown as a whole-region proxy; its sectors cannot be separated with the available map data.

properties.label: West Germany
properties.info: The Federal Republic of Germany joined NATO in 1955. Modern German state boundaries approximate the western federal territory.

properties.label: Saar
properties.info: The Saar Protectorate remained separate at the end of 1955. The Saar statute was rejected in a referendum that year; union with West Germany followed in 1957.

properties.label: Austria
properties.info: Austria regained full sovereignty under the State Treaty of 1955 and declared permanent neutrality. Vienna is shown as a whole-region proxy rather than divided occupation sectors.
